newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes strengthen in modest session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes strengthen in modest session.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes ended slightly firmer all around on Monday, making inroads against large losses posted last week, but momentum was fleeting due to light trading volume levels, traders said.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gained around 10 cents to talk late in the session at $19.20-30 a barrel, with the May/June WTI roll pegged around 7-10 cts.

Domestic grades switched hands sparingly, but were generally uplifted by news that Canada's Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc was forced to slice more than 1 million barrels per day of crude throughput due to a power outage in Minnesota.
Even though traders downplayed the effect IPL crude cuts had on the market as a whole, there was a definite push higher in sour differentials on those supply concerns.
"It was a slow day, so the grades rallied a bit on the news even if it isn't gaing to have a big impact," a cash crude trader said.
West Texas Sour/Midland departed Monday at a value of $2.30 below WTI/Cushing, 15 cts higher than on Friday.
Other grade trades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James move at a 37 cts discount to the marker, and exit the afternoon talked at 37-38 cts under level.
Midland/WTI was valued a few cents firmer at 33 cts under the marker, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire checking out at a $1.10 discount. HLS was the only grade to decline on the day, traders noted.
Recent talk of a Brent onslaught in the U.S. Gulf faded a shade on Monday, when barrels failed to appear, despite the market being flooded with foreign barrels of all types.
